Subject: Spike of 429s + latency from Redwood — causing checkouts to time out

Logan —

We started seeing a sudden spike of 429 responses and tail latency around 08:50 PT. Over the last 20 minutes ~8% of checkout tokenization requests are returning 429s and many others are taking >1.2s to complete; user checkout flows are timing out in our client. We attached a small sample (kitepay_error_samples_0529.csv) and a short log snippet.

This is impacting ~25% of production traffic for our EU customers routed through the us-west endpoint. We throttled on our side to reduce retries but the error rate is still high. Please advise immediate remediation and whether this will affect our SLA or ongoing rollout. We need a response within the hour — this is consumer-facing.

Thanks,
Samir

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 10:05:43 -07:00
Subject: Re: [KitePay] Spike of 429s + latency — initial technical readout and immediate mitigations

Quick technical summary after 15m of logs and metrics:
- Root cause (probable): per-tenant token-bucket configuration on the us-west route has burst_window set to 1s (legacy default) while the window for most of our tile/kv cache heuristics is 10s. The mismatch causes the bucket to refill too slowly for common request patterns (many short bursts), leading to frequent 429s when small bursts happen across many clients.
- Compounding factor: safety-valve auto-shed kicked in because prefix-caching estimates flagged increased effective QPS. That triggered a cross-tenant limiter we recently tightened in a config change shipped last week (config_diff_patch_v2.patch).
- Observed impact: 4xx (429) spike concentrated on tokenization and short-chat endpoints used by KitePay SDK (consistent with their samples). 95th latency increased from 280ms -> 1.3s for affected requests.

Immediate actions taken (live):
1) Rolled back the last-week cross-tenant limit override for the us-west route (rolled back at 10:02).
2) Increased per-tenant burst_window for KitePay from 1s -> 12s and applied a temporary extra_headroom flag to the tenant bucket (will auto-expire in 2 hours).
3) Opened a golden-route redirect rule to send 30% of traffic to the Dedicated pool (if capacity allows) as a staged mitigation.
4) Enabled more verbose token-bucket telemetry for KitePay for the next 2h so we can confirm steady state.

Next planned steps:
- Within 60m: if 429s drop below 0.5% and latency normalizes, keep the temporary settings and plan a config roll for all similarly-configured tenants.
- Post-mortem: add a validation check in config push that flags mismatch between burst_window and cache window heuristics.

Notes for customer comms: emphasize temporary rollback + staged routing to Dedicated; avoid deep internals.

Attachments: config_diff_patch_v2.patch, kb-log-snippet-0529.txt

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: [KitePay] Spike of 429s + latency — mitigation and next steps (summary)

Samir — quick summary of what we found and what we did:
- What happened: a recent config change created a mismatch between our per-tenant burst policy and the serving cache window, which caused token-bucket exhaustion and a spike of 429s for short-burst request patterns.
- Immediate remediation: we rolled back the cross-tenant tightening, temporarily increased KitePay's burst window (12s) and added a short-lived extra-headroom allowance. We also shifted a portion of traffic to a Dedicated pool while we validate behavior.
- Expected impact: you should see 429s return to baseline (<0.5%) and 95th latency return under 350ms within the next 15–30 minutes.
- Next steps: Marcus will monitor token-bucket telemetry and we'll follow up with a succinct post-mortem within 48 hours including a recommended config-validation guard.

We value the urgency — Vanessa will coordinate any SLA/credit conversation and I will keep you updated every 30 minutes until the metrics are stable.

Best,
Logan Wright
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
